During, the Democratic administration,
from 1885 to 1S80, the expenses of the
territorial prison amounted to $52,000 per
annum. During the first year under a
Republican regime, from March 4, 18S9,
to March 4, 1890, th6 expenses, with the
same number of prisoners, were $29,000.
It Is plain to any person who can read
and understand that the management
under the Democratic administration was
dishonest, and the management under a
Republican administration is honest.
That is all.
Di'Rrso three and a halt years of the
Ross boodle administration of the terri
torial penitentiary there was received
from the labor of convicts and the feeding
of United States prisoners the sum of
$7,500. During the first twelve months
of the present Republican administration
from March 4 1889, to March 4 1890,
(there being about the same number of
prisoners in the institution year per year,
from 13S3 to 1890) there was received the
amount of $8,000, from the same source.
Facts are facta and these facts mean that
the present administration of the terri
torial prison is honest and economical
and efficient, and that the Democratic
administration under ex-Gov. Ross was
dishonest, extravagant and inefficient.
Tin: admission of six new states in the
f ast year has had the effect of educating
the people somewhat. It has set them
to thinking ot what an unreasonable,
measely thing a territorial condition is.
How utterly out of place it is under the
rights guaranteed by the constitution of
the United States. The Boston Traveler
tersely puts it thus: "Territorial condi
tions are abnormal, according to the
American idea. The capacity and power
of a territorial population for self -government
is the all essential thing. That set
tled, the citizens of a territory have a
moral right to participation in the affairs
of the federal government. The United
States knows neither provinces nor colo
nies." A heneficial change in the military
branch of the government is under con
sideration at Washington. It is probable
that the present system of division com
manders will be abolished and instead
the affairs of the army will be adminis
tered through the various department
commanders. In the event of such an
arrangement the department of the Pacific
and the department of the Atlantic, the
most important stations, will be given
to the command of a major general,
the interior departments being com
manded by brigadier generals, who will
report direct to Major Gen. Schofield,
commanding at Washington. This ar
rangement would indeed prove of great
benefit over the present method. It
would do away with much of the red tape
now necessary and tend to localize mat
ters very materially.
The people of New Mexico must not
forget that under the Ross boodle admin
iatration, from 1885 to 1889, when this
territory was cursed with corrupt judges
and dishonest federal and territorial court
officials, the cost of running the courts
was $160,000 per year the people must
not forget that, oving to wise and bene
Itclal legislation passed by a Republican
legislature over the veto of that boodle
governor, put into office by Grover Cleve
land, and owing to a jusi aud honest ad
ministration of the courts, the entire ex
pense of their administration for the first
twelve months of the present Republican
regime, amounted to only $00,000, in
which sum there is included an estimate
ol a deficiency in the pay of jurors, etc.,
of about $10,000; this means that under
the Democratic administration the people
of New Mexico were systematically and
constantly robbed by corrupt judges and
dishonest court officials.

HANUFACTURINGr IN THE S0UTHWSST.
There is every reason for the belief that
ere many years have passed the south
west portion of the union will show a re
markable growth in the way of manu
factures. Particularly is this promised of
those towns which have now access to
the trade of Mexico through rail and
water connections. There ia a demand
for manufactured articlea in the south
west that the industrial world can not
longer overlook. It is almost near enough
to be counted a home market; it is
stable competition is not extensive, and
it is growing better year by year as the
people of Mexico progress. The exports
of Mexico amount to $00,000,000 yearly.
Of this sum $40,000,000 comes into the
United States, but instead of paying our
bills with manufactured articles we pay
in cash, and the money ia sent to En
gland, Germany and France, from which
countries most of Mexico's imports are
obtained. This should not be. It is not
reasonable to calculate that it can last
much longer. The time ia ripe for the
introduction of manufactories into the
southwest to correct this state cf things.
Fuel, cheap labol' and raw material are
quite easily had in this section, while the
market would seem to be one of absolute
certainty. All southwestern towns can
do no better than to call the attention of
manufacturers to these and similnr facts
w henever opportunity oilers.
ADVERTISE NEW MEXICO FRUIT,
Owing to the advanced seasons fruits
throughout the entire l!io Grande valley
iu New Mexico are ready for the market
from four to six weeks ahead of the Colo
rado products, and there is, therefore, a
safe market, near at hand, to the north
of us that ought to be nurtured by our
fruit growers. Early in October next
there is going to be an exposition held at
Pueblo, Colo., and arrangements have
been made for advertising it far and w ide,
the railroad companies taking special in
terest in working it up. The chances are
that people from all parts of the union
w ill be there, and we venture to suggest
that a more favorable opportunity than
this could scarcely be found for advant
ageously displaying samples of New Mex
ico's fruit products. Pueblo is easily ac
cessible by rail to New Mexico, and the
transportation companies will no doubt
make generous reductions. The choicest
fruits should be sent, lor Colorado is her
self going to make her best horticultural
display there.
BE NOT WEARY IN WELL DOING,
Union and organization will carry the
day for the Republicans at the coming
election. They have an honest and good
majority iu New Mexico, but the vote
must be brought out and polled. Union,
organization and work will do that. Work
has already commenced in the right di
rection, but a good deal more can be
done, than ia being done, and must be
done. Be up and be not weary in well
doing. The coming is the most im
portant election ever hold in the history
of New Mexico, as an integral part of this
union. The election of November 4
next, will decide whether advancement,
progress, coming wealth and an increas
ing population shall be invited by and
secured for New Mexico, or whether
retrogression, torpor and hostility to
the interests of the people shall for years
to come be the order of the day, and keep
capital and immigrants from our borders
and without our borders. The success
of the Republican party means the for
mer; the success of the Democratic basses
will bring about the latter.
THE SHAM OF THE DEMOCRATIC OPPO
SITION TO STATEHOOD.
The New York election law had to be
translated into nine different languages
for the enlightmeht of the voters of the
chief Democratic city of the country,
namely New York. There are 00,000
voters in New York, who either do not
at all understand the English language or
understand it very imperfectly. But
then New York is Democratic. In New
Mexico, where there are probably 10,000
voters w ho do not understand the English
language, but who are native born, and
who are good, loyal and honest citizens,
the Democratic party opposes the terri
tory's admission as a state, one of the
chief objections advanced by the poli
ticians, bosses and papers of that party,
being, tho alleged ignorance and the al
leged inability of the voting population
of thia territory to speak the English
language. Of course, this is the merest
pretense and rot. Were thia a Demo
cratic administration, had the Demo
cratic a majority in the present
congress, and did they believe,
that New Mexico would come in
as a Democratic state, they would pass
an enabling act between two days. The
reason for the opposition from the Demo
cratic bosses and ringster in New Moxico
ia simply brought about by the fear that
New Mexico would be Republican, elect
a Republican state government and send
Republican senators to congress. That
is all there is of it, and the seemingly
virtuous howl, that is raised by them at
the alleged ignorance of our people, at the
fact that many of our voters do not
speak the English language, at the
constitution and the apportionment, is
pretense, sham and a humbug, and they
know it. For a partisan advantage, they
slander and abuse the people of New
Mexico, lie about and conceal the great
natural resources of the territory and give
our people a bad name, whenever and
wherever they can, in congress and out of
congress, in their papers and in conversa
tion. However, it looks as if their nefarious
and scandalous proceedings would be in
vain; it looks, as if the constitution would
be adopted at the coming election; it looks
as if a Republican delegate would bo elec
ted, and if these two latter happen, it is
certain that a Republican congress will
pass an enabling act and that a Republi
can president will approve the same and
that on July 4, 1891, New Mexico will be
the forty-fifth state of the union.
SENATOR HENR7 M. TELLER,
The sentiment in favor of the re-election
of Senator Henry M. Teller is gain
ing strength daily and from all appear
ances Mr. Teller will be re-elected by a
handsome majority by the coming legis
lative assembly of the state of Colorado.
He is ono of the ablest men in the sena'e
he is a power in the senate; he is in
timately acquainted with public affairs
and tho needs of the great west and es
pecially of his owu state ho is true to his
friends and firm and courageous in his
convictions. Our people would be greatly
pleased should he be re-elected and sin
cerely hope, that he will be. In addition
to being extremely useful and beneficial
to the state, that has had the extreme
good sense to send him to the U. S. sen
ate, he has aided our people and helped
New Mexico whenever in his power. The
interests of the miner, of the stock raiser
and of the ranchman of New Mexico are
identical with those of the miner, the
stock raiser and the ranchman of Colo
rado what helps Colorado, more or less,
helps New Mexico. The recognition of
silver, the protection of the lead interests,
of the wool growers, of the cattle
raisers, of our farmers and fruit raisers,
our lumber men, are all of the greatest
good to New Mexico, for right there her
resources exist.
Senator Teller has done faithful, telling
and successful work for all these, and
hence the people of New Mexico, who un
fortunately for themselves, have no rep
resentation in congress (although they are
justly, fully and fairly entLled to two sen
ators and one congressman, and by rights
and in fairness ought to have had such
representation years ago) favor him for re
election to the United Statea senate, of
which body he has been for many years
one of the most prominent, able, suc
cessful aud honorable members.
